faq_heading: West Central Maple Ridge: your questions answered

blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. This section was written from the City of Maple Ridge's own pages and replaces text that was repeated word for word on the other Maple Ridge guides.
Port Haney: where West Central Maple Ridge began

Downtown Maple Ridge grew around Port Haney, a river landing on the north bank of the Fraser. The City says it is named after Thomas Haney, a brick maker who bought land there in 1879 because of the clay deposits. He ran a brickyard for 11 years. The river made it easy to ship bricks, and the CPR line helped the settlement grow quickly.

The river also shaped the street grid you see today. In early February 1880, part of the bank on the neighbouring Howison farm slid into the Fraser, partly blocking the river and sending waves through the wharves and piers. Fires hit Port Haney in 1910, 1926 and 1936. If you are looking at a home close to the river, that history is a good reason to read the floodplain and escarpment notes further down this page.
A heritage district you can walk

The City describes Port Haney as a heritage district, and some heritage buildings from other parts of Maple Ridge were moved here to keep them. Its Port Haney Heritage Walk links the main sites. It is about 1.4 km one way, rated moderate, with a few inclines.

blocks.text: Downtown on Saturdays and the rest of the week

Memorial Peace Park at 11930 224 Street is the middle of downtown. The Haney Farmers Market is held there. The City's 2024 listing showed Saturdays from 9:00 am to 2:00 pm, from April 27 to October 26. Dates change each year, so check the City's market page before you plan a visit.

The City lists five parks in the Port Haney area: Brickwood Park, Callaghan Park, Holly Park, Jim Hadgkiss Park and Storey Green Park. Ridge Meadows Hospital, the West Coast Express station and the Haney Place bus exchange are all in this part of the city too, which is why the area suits people who want services close at hand and a way to get to Vancouver without driving.
What the 2025 plan update means for owners

In its December 4, 2025 release, the City said council had finished a series of updates to the Official Community Plan and its area plans. For this part of the city, the Town Centre Area Plan now covers River Bend, uses 7 land use designations instead of 11, and adds a Town Centre Core designation for higher density in a walkable downtown. The City ties that core to the Haney Transit Exchange and the Port Haney West Coast Express station.

The City also says Maple Ridge needs 27,778 new homes by 2041. For an owner near the exchange or the station, that means the designation on your lot matters more than it used to. It can affect what could be built next door and what a buyer might pay for your site. Send me your address and I will look up the designation before you list or buy.
Floodplain and the Fraser escarpment

The City publishes floodplain maps for the Fraser and Alouette rivers. It shows the area expected to flood about once in 200 years and mails its Be Flood Ready guide to properties near the Fraser floodplain. The City says it manages flood risk case by case, and it has proposed a Floodplain Management Bylaw that would set clearer rules, including minimum building elevations.

The Fraser River Escarpment policy area runs from 207 Street in the west to 224 Street in the east, and from 124 Avenue down to the crest of the escarpment. I found no flood or slope statement written for West Central Maple Ridge as a whole, so check the map for any address near the river in Port Haney. Agricultural Land Reserve status is set parcel by parcel; check the Agricultural Land Commission map for larger lots.
Maple Ridge home prices, September 2026

The MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for a typical Maple Ridge home was $882,600 in September 2026, down 7.0% from a year earlier. Detached homes were $1,155,900 (down 7.7% over the year), townhouses $700,800 (down 8.1%) and apartments $513,400 (down 2.6%).

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 68 in June to 66 in September (−2.9%), and it took 8.5% of the city’s 188 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 83 in June to 78 in September (−6.0%), and it took 24.5% of the city’s 184 sales over the period.

faq.q: Is Port Haney part of West Central Maple Ridge?
faq.a: Port Haney is the historic river landing at the west end of downtown Maple Ridge. West Central is an MLS sub-area name and the City does not publish its boundary, so the closest official guides are the Town Centre Area Plan and the City's Port Haney neighbourhood page.

faq.q: Where is the Haney Farmers Market?
faq.a: In Memorial Peace Park at 11930 224 Street. The City's 2024 listing showed Saturdays, 9:00 am to 2:00 pm, from April 27 to October 26. Check the City's page for each year's dates.

faq.q: How do I get to Vancouver from West Central Maple Ridge?
faq.a: Haney Place Exchange is served by TransLink routes R3, 701, 733, 741, 743, 744, 745, 746, 748, 749 and 791. The West Coast Express stops at Port Haney Station (22300 River Road, no parking) and Maple Meadows Station, with five weekday trips in the morning and evening.

faq.q: Which Maple Ridge schools serve West Central?
faq.a: SD42 sets catchments by address and publishes no list for the MLS sub-area. Schools in the western and central parts of the city include Fairview, Laity View, Maple Ridge and Eric Langton elementary and Maple Ridge, Westview and Thomas Haney secondary. Confirm a specific address with SD42.

faq.q: Is West Central Maple Ridge in a floodplain?
faq.a: Parts of the city near the Fraser River are. The City publishes floodplain maps and mails its Be Flood Ready guide to properties near the floodplain. Rules differ lot by lot, so check the map for the exact address.

faq.q: What is changing in downtown Maple Ridge?
faq.a: The City's 2025 Town Centre Area Plan update added River Bend to the plan area, cut the land use designations from 11 to 7 and created a Town Centre Core designation for higher density around the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney station.

faq.q: Can a house here have a suite or more units?
faq.a: One secondary suite per lot inside the single detached building, up to 40% of the building's gross floor area and not in the floodplain area; eligible single-detached and duplex lots may also have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws.

faq.q: What plans shape West Central's future?
faq.a: The Town Centre Area Plan (first adopted November 2008, updated November 25, 2025 on the settled position in this program) covers the downtown core at the area's east edge, the Transit-Oriented Area Designation Bylaw No. 8001-2024 covers the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station TOAs, and TransLink's Langley–Haney Place BRT is in detailed planning. The guide page's claim that the Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan was adopted on January 27, 2026 conflicts with City sources showing only initial readings at the end of 2025; that conflict is recorded as a live-page error in Section 1 of this file.
